rv.q: "Home, I'm Darling" is a great comedy of the kind we don't see much anymore and ideal for a date night with plenty to argue about on the way home.
Every inch of set designer Courtney O’Neill’s set has mid-century flair, from the sun-colored kitchen to the texture of the upholstery.

Home, I'm Darling is a response to the overwhelming pace of the 24/7 world we've created, the fiscal disappointments of generations that can't reach the level of prosperity as adults that they grew up with, and the growing notion among Gen Z that life was simply better in earlier days.
What makes Home, I’m Darling so satisfying is the tension between its appealing premise and its uncomfortable implications as they roll out.
